statement: Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) describes archaeological offerings at Tenochtitlan's Templo Mayor and funerary urns assigned to Stage II around 1390 CE, in a complex whose paired shrines honored Huitzilopochtli and Tlaloc.

sources.citation: INAH, Museo del Templo Mayor, English exhibition text 'The Templo Mayor Museum', passages on the paired shrines and Stage II burial urns (1390 CE), https://lugares.inah.gob.mx/en/node/5284
sources.author: Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia
sources.access_note: Official museum page directly read. Stage II date attributed to museum's archaeological interpretation; object inventory details outside displayed text not inspected.

does_not_demonstrate: 1390 CE dates this identified building phase, not the origin of Mexica or broader Mesoamerican religion.
A paired state shrine does not imply that every community practiced identically.
Ritual offerings alone do not reconstruct the full content of lost spoken prayers or beliefs.
adversarial_counter: Archaeological interpretation of temple phases is distinct from evidence about state ideology and particular rituals.
notes: Institutional-source audit. Scope: named public page and its content only; no tradition founding-year inference. Independent historical / community review required before status change.
